adf.rationale: ADF on the level series with a fixed preregistered lag count (7, matching the documented weekly timing of the baseline) and autolag disabled: the lag count is never selected from the data, and the settings are recorded with the result instead of a pass/fail label (docs/ECONOMETRIC_METHODOLOGY.md 'Specification decision tree' step 2).

kpss.rationale: KPSS on the level series with a fixed preregistered lag count (7) as the complement of ADF (null of stationarity); short-sample disagreement between ADF and KPSS is recorded as a warning, never resolved by choosing the convenient answer.

ljung_box.rationale: Small lags 3 and the baseline weekly timing 7 (docs/ECONOMETRIC_METHODOLOGY.md 'Estimation and diagnostics': Ljung-Box at justified small lags); model_df consumes the design's estimated parameter count (intercept plus slopes), so the smallest declared lag must exceed it - lags 1/2 would have non-positive adjusted dof and are not declared instead of being reported as undefined.

heteroskedasticity.rationale: Breusch-Pagan is the methodology's named example ('Estimation and diagnostics'); the fitted design columns are the heteroskedasticity regressors, no extra series is introduced, and the preregistered response to a rejection is the already-declared HAC covariance - no reweighting, no outlier removal.

influence.rationale: Cook's distance from the plain OLS fit (leverage/residual geometry, independent of the HAC covariance) with the conventional 4/nobs flagging threshold taken from this config; flagged observations are reported with dates and never removed without an operational reason and a with/without report.

sensitivity_presets.rationale: Preregistered HAC lag sensitivity (docs/ECONOMETRIC_METHODOLOGY.md 'Estimation and diagnostics': baseline maxlags 7, sensitivity 3 and 14 when the sample supports it); a fixed alternative lag count, never selected from the data.

Preregistered HAC lag sensitivity (docs/ECONOMETRIC_METHODOLOGY.md 'Estimation and diagnostics': baseline maxlags 7, sensitivity 3 and 14 when the sample supports it); a fixed alternative lag count, never selected from the data.

Preregistered source sensitivity: re-estimation on the parallel dashboard-reported provider series (same metric definitions, alternate source dimension). The variant is a robustness check, never a second result; both sources share Dune lineage, so agreement is not independent confirmation.

Preregistered price-mark sensitivity: re-estimation with every bound price-basis series moved to the end-of-day mark (docs/ECONOMETRIC_METHODOLOGY.md 'Preparation and transform policy': alternate daily price marks). It applies only where a bound variable is valued through a declared daily price basis; a model whose variables are provider-reported USD as-is records the preset as not applicable instead of inventing a variant.
